transcript.text: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A swollen, very hot or chemical-smelling battery can catch fire. Stop using and charging it now, unplug the charger, and if it is safe to move put it somewhere non-flammable away from anything that could burn. Don't puncture, squeeze or try to open the battery, and don't put it in the household bin — take it to a battery recycling point. No, do not use it or charge it again. A battery that gets extremely hot and has swollen to the point of splitting its casing is a serious safety hazard and could catch fire. This indicates an internal cell failure rather than a simple charging issue. You must stop using the vacuum immediately and dispose of the damaged battery safely at a local household waste recycling centre or via your retailer's battery return scheme.

Ok, understood. It's still clicked into the vacuum and leaning against the kitchen cupboards next to the tea towels, with a faint chemical smell. Should I move it somewhere else, and is it safe to take it out?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, move it immediately. Do not try to remove the battery from the vacuum body yourself; prying it out could puncture the swollen cells and trigger a fire. Instead, carefully lift or slide the entire vacuum unit (with the battery still attached) away from the cupboards and tea towels into an open, non-flammable area like a garage, shed, or outside on concrete, keeping it away from anything that can burn. Once it is in a safe spot, leave it alone—do not charge it, do not use it, and do not attempt to disassemble it. This level of heat and physical deformation indicates a critical internal failure that requires professional disposal.

candidates: Failed battery cell causing thermal runaway (high)

You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Shark; model IZ201UK.
The fault they reported is: "battery got really hot on charge and looks puffed up with plastic case split at the seam". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
